subject: biology-hl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Gene expression
bigPicture: Every cell has the same genome but expresses a different set of genes. Transcription factors, mRNA lifetime and epigenetic tags decide which genes are used, and the environment can shift those tags without changing the DNA sequence.

keyIdeas.answer: The way information in a gene affects the phenotype, usually through transcription, translation and the action of the protein (e.g. an enzyme).
Proteins called transcription factors bind to specific DNA sequences: promoters, where RNA polymerase binds, and enhancers, which can be some distance away. This increases or decreases transcription.

keyIdeas.cue: How does mRNA breakdown regulate translation?
keyIdeas.answer: Nucleases break mRNA down. In human cells mRNA can last from minutes to days, and the longer it lasts the more protein is made.
The development of patterns of differentiation in a multicellular organism through changes in gene expression. The DNA base sequence is unchanged, so the phenotype changes but not the genotype.

Genome: all the DNA of an organism. Transcriptome: all the RNA transcribed in a cell at a given time. Proteome: all the proteins made. No cell expresses all its genes, and the pattern decides how it differentiates.

keyIdeas.cue: Give two epigenetic tags and their effects.
keyIdeas.answer: Methylation of cytosine in a promoter represses transcription of that gene. Methylation of amino acids in histones can repress or activate transcription.

keyIdeas.cue: How can epigenetic changes be inherited?
keyIdeas.answer: If tags such as DNA methylation or histone modifications stay in place through mitosis or meiosis, a changed phenotype can pass to daughter cells or offspring without any change to the DNA sequence.

keyIdeas.cue: Give an environmental effect on gene expression.
keyIdeas.answer: Exposure to air pollution is associated with changes in the methyl tags on DNA.

keyIdeas.cue: Why are ligers and tigons different?
keyIdeas.answer: Most, but not all, epigenetic tags are removed from eggs and sperm. Some imprinted genes keep tags that depend on which parent they came from. A liger (lion father, tigress mother) grows much larger than either parent, while a tigon (tiger father, lioness mother) doesn't, because growth genes are imprinted differently in each species.

keyIdeas.cue: What do monozygotic twin studies show?
keyIdeas.answer: Identical twins have the same genome, so differences between them (which often increase with age) show the environment's effect on gene expression, e.g. different methylation patterns.

keyIdeas.cue: Give external factors that change gene expression.
keyIdeas.answer: A hormone, e.g. a steroid hormone binding a receptor that changes transcription of target genes. A biochemical in bacteria: lactose switches on the genes for lactose use in E. coli (operon names not required).

keyTerms.def: Protein that binds DNA to regulate transcription.
Chemical mark (e.g. methyl group) changing gene expression, not sequence.
All RNA transcribed in a cell at a given time.
All proteins produced by a cell or organism.

workedExamples.title: Interpret a twin study
workedExamples.prompt: Twin A smokes and twin B doesn't. At age 50 their methylation patterns differ much more than at age 3. Explain.
steps: Same genome, so the differences aren't genetic.
Changes build up over a lifetime.
So gene expression and phenotype diverge.
workedExamples.answer: The environment causes epigenetic differences that increase with age.

misconceptions.right: They change gene expression, not the base sequence.

misconceptions.wrong: All cells express all their genes at low levels.
misconceptions.right: Cells express only a subset. That is what makes cell types differ.
Promoter methylation represses, but histone methylation can activate or repress.

practice.prompt: Distinguish between genome, transcriptome and proteome.
checkpoints: Genome: all genes/DNA, the same in all cells
Transcriptome: RNA made at a given time; varies
Proteome: proteins made; varies with cell type

practice.prompt: Explain how DNA methylation can control gene expression.
checkpoints: Methyl groups added to cytosine in the promoter
Transcription factors / RNA polymerase can't bind
